pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql; test/done.test.js 'AC-1' checks all existing items are 0 and the CHECK rejects 2.
'AC-2' test covers / and ?view=open, filtering and id order.
'AC-3' marks 3 then 1 done and expects ✓ items in id order.
'AC-5' asserts exact nav HTML for each view and for /.
'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for several values, including __proto__ and the empty string.
'AC-7' and the Empty table, Nothing open and Nothing done state tests.

traffic/routes.json has the routes, but the only test naming AC-8 was deleted in commit b9986fd 'Follow-up edits'. No remaining test checks routes.json, so nothing would fail if the routes were removed.

findings.what: The last commit (b9986fd, 'Follow-up edits', by a bot) deleted the 'AC-8: synthetic traffic requests the done and all views' test. AC-8 now has no test naming it, and the spec does not mark it 'verified by review'. The routes.json change is unguarded.
findings.fix: Restore the AC-8 test (or an equivalent that reads traffic/routes.json and asserts both routes). Explain any removal with a spec decision.

findings.what: The body says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' and that test/done.test.js covers AC-1 to AC-8. Both are false: the final commit deleted the AC-8 test.
findings.fix: Restore the test, or correct the PR body to say what was removed and why.

findings.what: The deletion left a stray blank line before the closing `});` of the describe block at line 73.

lenses.note: A spec exists; the change implements the views, with AC-8 untested.
7 of 8 items are met and every state row has a test. AC-8 has no test after the last commit.
Tests were not run (they need the workers vitest pool; CI is declared). The AC-8 test was deleted in the last commit.
README describes the views. traffic/routes.json is described in the README and still accurate.
The view lookup uses Object.hasOwn, so __proto__ is rejected. The queries are static strings. Nothing else found.
The view value is checked against an allowlist and titles are escaped. The traffic route regex now allows '?' but still refuses spaces and '#'.
Only a minimal server-rendered HTML page changed; there is no UI framework or styling files.
No browser or screenshots are available; the page is plain server-rendered HTML.
The 'no tests deleted' and 'covers AC-1 to AC-8' claims are false.
